mately 200 mg of urate is excreted daily in the feces. This phenomenon ensures that levels of ATP do not ﬂuctuate in concert
with the dietary intake of purines, or may represent an important evolutionary development to protect the integrity of cellular DNA.
On the other hand, pyrimidine ribonucleoside monophosphates (NMPs) and ribonucleosides are absorbed readily from the
intestine and utilized for nucleic acid synthesis. This has been demonstrated by studies of humans with hereditary oroticaciduria,
a rare defect in conversion of orotic acid to uridine monophosphate (UMP) in de novo pyrimidine synthesis. Such patients have
